Title: Claude Code's API billing depends on how often the cache expires
HN text: Hello, HN! I’m Max, CTO at Hystax. We use Claude a lot in our development work, and we’re also trying to make coding agents cheaper to run. We built the open-source Kompressor for compressing identical tool outputs that agents constantly resend. In our Codex tests, we noticed a real cost reduction of 22.7%. But testing it with Claude Code, we found something completely different. In Claude Code, the cache plays a more crucial role than compression. Claude Code marks its messages with caching points. As a result, almost every request consists of a long cached prefix and a new, truncated final part. Based on practical experience with Opus 5.5, reading from the cache appears to cost $0.20 per million tokens, accounting for about 92–95% of the tokens charged for prompts. AI Security Issues Are Social Engineering Issues
Capability-Based Security is part of the fix
When I was at EFF in the 2010s, I spent a lot of time fretting about the fundamental security of networked devices. Apart from the usual concerns, I struggled to imagine a transition to a redecentralized future with fragile personal computers and servers. Peter Eckersley , my co-worker and frequent conversation partner, shared my concern, but had another reason to be worried. He believed that future near-superintelligent AIs would soon be used to discover and exploit security flaws across the whole ecosystem.

Title: A lawyer used AI to write a report, but billed full time. What should I do?
HN text: This is not a request for legal advice, and therefore the country matters little here. I write because I am interested in hearing opinions on the moral implications of something that is bound to happen more and more often. Context: A lawyer wrote a report for me. Not only was it was of poor quality, but he billed a surprising number of hours for it. I then noticed that one of the references was completely made up, typical of AI hallucination. I started pulling on the thread and slowly became convinced that he had almost certainly heavily relied on AI and inflated his hours. We went to the first judicial level, and the judge rejected out of hand the various strands of evidence that I presented.
